key_insight: Batching parameter-shift evaluations into each quantum job reduced QNN training job counts versus SPSA under matched job and shot budgets.
engineering_relevance: Optimizer design can amortize cloud quantum queue overhead by extracting more useful training progress from each processor interaction.
method: Compare optimizers with equal job counts and shots per job, varying how each job is filled.
Batch parameter-shift stencils fixed before submission to estimate gradients.
Test a structure-aware stencil search that interprets circuit responses as sinusoids.
evidence_signal: For 24–48 parameters, simulations required 20–50% as many jobs as SPSA; across three interleaved IBM ibm_fez runs at six and eight qubits, the batched optimizer matched SPSA’s 50-job final training loss within 4–20 jobs.
watch_item: Hardware evidence is limited to six and eight qubits; test accuracy improved clearly only at eight qubits, with no significant difference at six.
paper_title: Training quantum neural networks one job at a time
